text:
sarah: quick check — partner wants us to connect to their service via an interface VPC endpoint in our prod VPC. do we still need outbound NAT for their egress? also: will their IPs show up in our logs (we need to know for redaction)
raj: if it's an AWS interface endpoint (ENI-backed) traffic stays in the VPC to the service endpoint, no internet NAT required. route table must have the endpoint ENIs reachable and SG allow outbound to the endpoint SG. :white_check_mark:
elaine: +1 on raj. but be careful: some partner integrations call out to third-party domains from inside that flow. confirm with partner that there are no downstream external calls. if there are, those would require NAT/egress rules.
sarah: good point — i've asked partner, waiting. on logs: do we redact destination IPs by default? we need to avoid storing partner internal IPs in long-term logs.
elaine: our default is to keep flow logs + app logs, but we have a redaction pipeline for PII and partner IPs. add a pipeline rule in datadog/ingest: `drop_fields: ["destination.ip"]` or `mask_regex: {"destination.ip": "REDACTED"}` depending on retention needs. i can open a PR with the exact rule.
raj: for infra-level VPC flow logs we can also set sampling or ship to a short retention S3 bucket with lifecycle. if you want full fidelity for 7 days only, we do that -> move to s3://redwood-flowlogs/temp/ and lifecycle 7d. longer retention requires an approved data classification.
sarah: ok can we get an exception to keep 7d raw and redact destination.ip before archival? can someone approve that here so i can update terraform?
elaine: approve for 7d raw -> redact before long-term store. @infra-bot please create a ticket and tag security-audit. :thumbsup:
infra-bot: Created ticket INF-2026: "partner vpc endpoint logging lifecycle + redaction" and linked to PR template. assignees: raj, elaine. ETA: EOW.
sarah: thanks — one more: partner asked for a temporary SSH bastion rule from their IP (source x.x.x.x/32) to our jump host for onboarding (48h). any objections?
raj: need justification + expiration and least-privileges. ok if it's 48h, source locked to that CIDR, port 22 only, and we add an AWS Config rule to check removal after 48h. also log the SSH certificate use.
elaine: add a short scoped runbook: who will remove the rule and how we verify. i'll review the terraform change.
sarah: i'll open the PR with terraform change (security-group change + aws config rule). tagging here when done. :eyes:
raj: quick nit — use `var.partner_onboard_window = "48h"` not a hard-coded timestamp so we can rotate easily in future.
sarah: noted. PR coming in a few mins. thanks all.
